verdict.rationale: LiteLLM's gateway Router has documented routing rules: load-balancing across deployments, retries, cooldowns, and fallbacks to other model groups. A failing model or provider automatically fails over to a healthy backup, and content-policy violations can route to fallback models, so availability-driven switching mid-task is clearly delivered. missing for 10: documented cost-based routing rules, explicit capability-based routing beyond a marketing line, independent or hands-on corroboration of mid-task switching.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my agent can switch models mid-task by policy — cost, capability, or availability — through gateway routing rules

citations.quote: If a call fails after num_retries, LiteLLM falls back to another model group, so a failing model or provider automatically fails over to a healthy backup.
litellm proxy will loop through all the model_groups specified in `fallbacks=["gpt-3.5-turbo"]`
